newsitem.title: UK: UK "wise man" Minford calls for 1/2 point rate cut.
newsitem.headline: UK "wise man" Minford calls for 1/2 point rate cut.

text.p: UK "wise man" Professor Patrick Minford told Reuters in an interview that UK monetary policy was too tight and base lending rates should be cut in two stages to 5.25 percent.
"I think the economy is still recovering and any rise in interest rates would be premature...I think rates should be cut by half a point to 5.25 percent," Minford said.
He also said sterling's rally was a result of monetary policy being too tight and he would favour a retreat in the sterling exchange rate to levels seen before its recent upturn.
Minford said if monetary policy was eased, it would pave the way for sterling exchange rates to fall.
His view is contrary to fellow "wise man" Tim Congdon who on Friday said he would like to see rates rise by 100 basis points.
Both men are members of the UK Treasury's panel of independent forecasters which was set up in the wake of sterling's exit from the Exchange Rate Mechanism in 1992.
The panel will submit its next report to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke before the November budget.
